ORDER granting 17 Motion for Leave to Proceed in forma pauperis. Beginning on September 3, 2026, Plaintiffs in all of these consolidated cases - except the lead case, 26-CV-5329 - filed motions for leave to proceed in forma pauperis. See, e.g., Carrillo et al. v. Samuels et al., 26-CV-5330, ECF No. 19 (S.D.N.Y. Sept. 4, 2026). That same day, the Court ordered the DOE to file a letter on this docket no later than September 9, 2026, indicating whether it intended to oppose any of those motions and stated that if DOE failed to file a letter by that date, it would grant the motions as unopposed. See ECF No. 82. The DOE has not filed any letter to date. Accordingly, Plaintiffs' motions for leave to proceed in forma pauperis are hereby GRANTED as unopposed. The Clerk of Court is directed to docket this Order in all cases listed in the Appendix to ECF No. 54 and to terminate the identical motions to proceed in forma pauperis filed in all cases listed in that Appendix. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Jesse M. Furman on 9/10/2026) (ar) (Entered: 09/10/2026) Order on Motion for Leave to Proceed In Forma Pauperis

OPINION AND ORDER: At bottom, the crux of Plaintiffs' theory is that by signing a contract, a parent and private school can compel a federal court to issue an order directing a school district to circumvent its ordinary payment procedures and ma ke pendency payments to their preferred providers on their preferred timelines and in their preferred amounts - never to be recouped, even if the school district ultimately prevails on the merits. Neither logic nor the law requires that result. Accor dingly, and for the reasons stated above, Plaintiffs motions for a preliminary injunction are GRANTED in part and DENIED in part as set forth in the Court's July 31, 2026 Order, ECF No. 54, as modified in its Order issued later that same day, EC F No. 56. Taking a step back, the tactics of iBrain and LFLG in these cases and others should give one pause. For years, they have sought to exploit several structural quirks of the IDEA's stay-put provision (and judicial interpretation thereof) : that it creates an entitlement to an "automatic injunction"; that it does not require administrative exhaustion; and that payments made by a school district pursuant to it are not recoupable. These efforts make plain that the goal is for iBrain and LFLG to get as much taxpayer money from the DOE as they can, as quickly as they can, safe in the knowledge that they will not have to give the money back even if the DOE ultimately prevails. ORDER granting in part and denying in part 6 Motion for TRO; granting in part and denying in part 6 Motion for Preliminary Injunction. For reasons that will be explained at greater length in an Opinion to follow, the Court hereby ORDERS as fol lows herein. The June 30, 2026 temporary restraining order, see ECF No. 18, is hereby VACATED. As noted, the Court will file an Opinion more fully explaining its reasons for these rulings in due course. In the meantime, the parties shall confer and, no later than August 7, 2026, file a joint letter providing their views on what, if anything, remains in these cases to resolve and proposing any next steps. For convenience, an Appendix is attached to this Order identifying which cases fall into th e categories discussed above. The Clerk of Court is directed to docket this Order in all cases listed in the Appendix, to terminate ECF No. 6 in Donohue v. Samuels et al., No. 26-CV-5329 (JMF), and to terminate the identical motions filed in all cases listed in the Appendix. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Jesse M.
